ActionRiskClassification.description: Operator-reviewed business risk for one executable action.
ActionRiskClassification.title: ActionRiskClassification

Anchor.description:
Redundant evidence for locating a step's target on screen.

Resolution ladder consumes fields in order of preference (strongest, most
drift-tolerant first): ``structural`` (DOM / UIA element, when the backend
supports it) -> template (local, then global) -> ocr_text -> landmarks ->
grounder. ``structural`` is the deterministic top rung; the remaining
(visual) rungs are the FALLBACK floor for pixel-only substrates.

template.description: Bundle-relative path to the PNG crop
template.title: Template

structural.description: STRUCTURAL locator (DOM selector / role+name, or UIA AutomationId / role+name) of the clicked target, captured at record time when the recording backend exposes it (openadapt_flow.backend.StructuralActionBackend). Drives the structural ACTION rung -- the TOP of the resolution ladder -- which re-finds the SAME element deterministically (no pixel match) and is far more drift-tolerant than the visual rungs (21/21 vs 6/21 on the desktop benchmark). None on pixel-only substrates or bundles compiled before this capability; the ladder then resolves via the visual rungs below.

region.description: Crop location in the recorded frame
region.title: Region

click_point.description: Click point in the recorded frame
click_point.title: Click Point

ocr_text.description: Text label at/near the target, if any
ocr_text.title: Ocr Text

context_text.description: Identity evidence: OCR text on the target's row (full-width band at the crop's height) EXCLUDING the target's own crop and timestamp-bearing lines. Verified before every click (see runtime.identity); None when the band had no usable text at compile time.
context_text.title: Context Text

structured_identity.description: STRUCTURED identity text (DOM / accessibility tree) of the clicked target's row, captured at record time when the recording backend exposes it (openadapt_flow.backend.IdentityBackend.structured_text_at). The REAL characters (a genuine digit 0 vs a letter O), so replay verifies identity by exact/normalized string compare with NO OCR ambiguity -- the structured-text tier of the identity ladder (see runtime.identity). None on pixel-only substrates or bundles recorded before this capability; the ladder then falls back to the OCR context_text tier.
structured_identity.title: Structured Identity

record_key.description: Stable record id of the target's row at record time (plaintext, compile-time only). The PHI-free pass hashes it into ``identity_template.record_key`` and clears this field.
record_key.title: Record Key

structured_row.description: Whether ``structured_identity`` came from a record row (compile-time only; moved to ``identity_template.structured_row``).
structured_row.title: Structured Row

structured_ambiguous.description: Whether teach time saw another row read the same with no record id between them (compile-time only; moved to ``identity_template.teach_ambiguous``).
structured_ambiguous.title: Structured Ambiguous

identity_template.description: PHI-FREE identity template (salted-hash + shape) of the recorded context band and structured identity. When present, the runtime verifies target identity from THIS (no plaintext name/DOB/MRN in the artifact — the PHI audit's REM-2) and ``context_text`` / ``structured_identity`` are None. Bundles compiled before this capability carry the plaintext fields instead and still replay unchanged (backward compatible). See openadapt_flow.runtime.identity_template.

identifier_crop.description: Bundle-relative PNG crop of the target row's DISCRIMINATIVE IDENTIFIER cell (the MRN / name+DOB region), emitted by the COMPILER (templates/identifiers/<step>.png -- under templates/ so it is sealed with the other image crops in an encrypted bundle) for identity-armed steps that captured no structured text (Citrix / RDP / remote-display pixel recordings), or for any step whose identifier region was explicitly marked at record time (--identifier). Feeds the pixel-compare and optional VLM tiers of the identity ladder (see runtime.identity): the rendered PIXELS retain the O/0 and l/1 distinction OCR collapses, so a crop-vs-crop compare catches the glyph-collapse wrong-patient where the DOM/a11y tree is unavailable. None on structured (browser/UIA) recordings unless marked (the structured tier owns identity there; no identity pixels at rest) and on bundles compiled before this capability -- Step.identifier_crop_missing_reason records WHY; the ladder then falls through to the OCR band tier.
identifier_crop.title: Identifier Crop

identifier_region.description: Location of `identifier_crop` in the recorded frame (x, y, w, h). Replay re-crops the SAME box at the resolved point (translated by the recorded region's offset from the recorded click point, exactly as the OCR band's exclude region is) so the pixel/VLM tiers compare like-for-like. Set iff `identifier_crop` is set.
identifier_region.title: Identifier Region

dialog_region.description: Box of the active dialog (the topmost modal) that held the target in the recorded frame, when it sat in one. The context band was cut to it, so text of the page behind the dialog is not identity evidence. Replay cuts the live band to the live dialog's box, and fails the identity check closed when no dialog holds the resolved point. None outside a dialog and on bundles compiled before this capability.
dialog_region.title: Dialog Region

dialog_row.description: True reads the target's own row inside dialog_region. False permits the whole dialog when teach time positively found a standalone control with no usable row text; replay must confirm no record row again. None conservatively uses the target's row.
dialog_row.title: Dialog Row

form_identity.description: A labelled save on a create-new form: before the click, its form must hold exactly the fields this run typed, with the values typed. See FormIdentity. None everywhere else.

search_pad.description: Pixels of padding around `region` for the local search
search_pad.title: Search Pad

Anchor.title: Anchor

ApiAdmission.description:
A person's acceptance of a compiler-proposed API step.

Bound to the exact binding by :attr:`spec_digest`; a changed binding needs
a new admission. Only a person can admit (an agent, model or service name
admits nothing).
ApiAdmission.title: ApiAdmission

ApiBinding.description:
A declarative API/tool call that performs a step's write WITHOUT the GUI.

The TOP of the capability ladder (RFC ``docs/design/WORKFLOW_PROGRAM_IR.md``
section 4, the ``api`` implementation of a ``TransitionContract``): where the
target app exposes a real API, driving its GUI to make the same write is the
wrong tool. When a step carries an ``ApiBinding`` AND the run configures an
:class:`~openadapt_flow.runtime.actuators.ApiActuator`, the runtime performs
the write by CALLING the API deterministically (``$0``, zero model calls),
confirms it with the same
:class:`~openadapt_flow.runtime.effects.EffectVerifier` that gates a GUI
write, and SKIPS the GUI resolution/act for that step. This is the
``api`` leaf of the same contract the structural rung realizes as ``dom_uia``
and the visual ladder realizes as ``vision_rdp`` -- one semantic effect,
backend-specific implementation.

ADDITIVE and back-compatible: the field is optional and defaults absent, so a
bundle carrying no binding replays EXACTLY as today (GUI actuation). A binding
also defaults to GUI fallback when the API tier is unavailable before
delivery. A workflow can instead set ``on_unavailable="halt"`` to declare an
API-only action. That mode refuses before GUI resolution or input rather than
inventing a second, unqualified actuation path.

Fields are REST/JSON-first but shaped so a FHIR / MCP / tool binding fits the
same model (``kind`` selects the substrate; a FHIR resource POST, an MCP tool
invocation, and a plain REST write all reduce to method + endpoint + body +
the expected effect). Placeholders ``{param}`` in the URL / query / body are
substituted from the run's typed params (``Workflow.params`` overlaid by the
caller's values) at actuation time.

kind.description: Substrate: 'rest'/'fhir' HTTP, an 'mcp'/'tool' call, or 'web_form': a browser form save repeated through the live session
kind.title: Kind

on_unavailable.description: Pre-delivery API-unavailability policy. 'gui' preserves the back-compatible GUI fallback; 'halt' declares this step API-only and refuses without GUI input when no actuator is configured or the actuator proves that no request was sent.
on_unavailable.title: On Unavailable

method.description: HTTP verb (REST/FHIR) or logical operation name (mcp/tool)
method.title: Method

url_template.description: Endpoint template; absolute (http...) or relative to the actuator's base_url. `{param}` placeholders are substituted from the run's typed params.
url_template.title: Url Template

body_template.description: JSON request body template; string leaves may carry `{param}` placeholders substituted from the run's params.
body_template.title: Body Template

query.description: Query-string params; values may carry `{param}` too
query.title: Query

headers.description: Extra request headers; values may carry `{param}`
headers.title: Headers

expected_status.description: Explicit acceptable HTTP status codes; empty means any 2xx is success (anything else is treated as an attempted write of unknown effect and HALTs -- never GUI-retried).
expected_status.title: Expected Status

timeout_s.description: Per-request timeout in seconds
timeout_s.title: Timeout S

effects.description: The system-of-record effect(s) this call is expected to produce. Used to CONFIRM the API write via the run's EffectVerifier when the step itself declares no `effects` (an API write must be confirmable, exactly as a GUI write with declared effects is).
effects.title: Effects

identity.description: Exact run-parameter bindings that prove qualified record identity for API actuation. Each binding must occur in both the request template and an effect selector before the request may be sent.
identity.title: Identity

web_form.description: The recorded form save, for kind='web_form' only

admission.description: A person's acceptance of a compiler-proposed binding. A web_form binding never runs without one.

ApiBinding.title: ApiBinding

ApiIdentityBinding.description:
Exact API request/effect binding for one qualified identity signal.

``param`` must be referenced by the outgoing request template and by
``effect_field`` through ``ValueExpr(param=...)``. Runtime validates both
sides before any request is sent, so an API optimization cannot bypass the
qualified identity contract that guards the equivalent GUI action.

request_pointers.description: Explicit target-bearing JSON pointers in the request template. Supported roots are /url/<effect-field>, /body/..., and /query/...; the terminal pointer segment must name the bound effect field, and headers are never accepted as target identity.
request_pointers.title: Request Pointers

ApiIdentityBinding.title: ApiIdentityBinding

BackendHints.description:
Trusted local execution target captured with a remote-display demo.

These hints bind a window-scoped recording to the same local client window
at replay time. They live only inside ``workflow.json``: plaintext in an
explicitly unencrypted local bundle, or encrypted with the rest of a sealed
bundle. They never enter the plaintext manifest or PHI-free hosted report
rail because a window title can contain a patient or account name.

The schema is deliberately closed to the two pixel-window substrates that
use ``BackendConfig.rdp_*``.  Network endpoints, credentials, arbitrary
backend configuration, and provider-specific recipes are not recording
metadata and must still come from the deployment config.
BackendHints.title: BackendHints

BundleManifest.description:
Integrity + provenance manifest for a compiled bundle (schema v2).

Sealed on :meth:`Workflow.save` and re-verified on :meth:`Workflow.load`
(``openadapt_flow.bundle_validation``): ``file_hashes`` is a SHA-256 per
template/image asset (bundle-relative path -> hex digest), ``content_digest``
is a whole-bundle SHA-256 over the manifest-free ``workflow.json`` content
AND those asset hashes (so it changes if any semantic byte changes), and
``provenance`` carries the compiler version + certification block. ``encrypted``
mirrors ``Workflow.encrypted``: True when the bundle is sealed at rest with
AES-256-GCM -- both ``workflow.json`` and every ``templates/*.png`` crop.
The ``file_hashes`` are always digests over the PLAINTEXT asset (sealed
BEFORE encryption), so integrity re-verifies against the decrypted crops.
A v1 bundle carries no manifest. Verified loading requires a persisted
integrity seal rather than computing a replacement for unsealed content.

file_hashes.description: bundle-relative asset path -> SHA-256 hex digest
file_hashes.title: File Hashes

BundleManifest.title: BundleManifest

BundleProvenance.description:
Who produced a bundle and, if certified, under what policy (schema v2).

``compiler_version`` records the ``openadapt_flow`` version that compiled /
last saved the bundle, so an operator inventory can tell which compiler an
artifact came from. The certification block is populated only for a bundle
that passed a policy certification (see :meth:`Workflow.stamp_certification`
/ ``openadapt_flow.policy.evaluate_policy``): ``policy_name`` is the policy
it was certified against, ``certification_status`` is a short label
(``"certified"`` / ``"failed"`` / ``"expired"``), and ``expires_at`` is an
optional ISO expiry after which a consumer should re-certify. An
uncertified bundle leaves the block at its defaults.

compiler_version.description: openadapt_flow version that produced the bundle
compiler_version.title: Compiler Version

source_recording_sha256.description: Exact approved sanitized recording archive used for compilation
source_recording_sha256.title: Source Recording Sha256

sanitized_from_digest.description: Verified source bundle content digest for a sanitized derivative
sanitized_from_digest.title: Sanitized From Digest

compiler_config_sha256.description: Canonical digest of the compiler options used for this bundle
compiler_config_sha256.title: Compiler Config Sha256

created_at.description: When this manifest/provenance was first sealed (ISO 8601)
created_at.title: Created At

policy_name.description: Certified bundle: the policy it was certified against
policy_name.title: Policy Name

certified.description: Whether the bundle passed policy certification
certified.title: Certified

certified_at.description: ISO timestamp of the certification, if any
certified_at.title: Certified At

expires_at.description: Optional ISO expiry; a consumer should re-certify after it
expires_at.title: Expires At

certification_invalidated_at.description: ISO timestamp when a previously persisted certification stopped matching this bundle contract
certification_invalidated_at.title: Certification Invalidated At

certification_invalidation_reason.description: PHI-free reason the persisted certification was invalidated; the bundle must be certified again before production use
certification_invalidation_reason.title: Certification Invalidation Reason

governed_authorization_template.description: Value-free, hash-bound production authorization template for this exact certified bundle

BundleProvenance.title: BundleProvenance

BusinessDecisionEvidenceRequirement.description:
One reviewed evidence item required before a business answer is valid.

The answer carries only a digest of the retained local artifact.  It does
not carry screenshots, record values, or free text across a trust boundary.
BusinessDecisionEvidenceRequirement.title: BusinessDecisionEvidenceRequirement

BusinessDecisionOption.description: One finite answer and its exact compiled successor.
BusinessDecisionOption.title: BusinessDecisionOption

BusinessDecisionSpec.description:
A finite, reviewed human decision inside a workflow program.

This is not an identity or effect verifier.  It only selects a declared
branch and binds a declared output.  The successor action still runs the
normal fresh-frame, identity, policy, postcondition, and effect gates.
BusinessDecisionSpec.title: BusinessDecisionSpec

ChoiceOptionShape.description:
What the demonstrated option looked like among its siblings.

Replay finds the option list by shape, never by position: elements with
``role`` (``option`` or ``treeitem``), or, for a list without ARIA, the
``tag`` and every class in ``classes`` (the classes the chosen option
shared with the other options in its list; none for a list of bare
items). Only elements that appeared after the control opened count.
ChoiceOptionShape.title: ChoiceOptionShape

ConcatTemplate.description:
Precomputed SPLIT-match key (consecutive recorded tokens the live OCR
may glue into one), since hashes cannot be concatenated at replay.
ConcatTemplate.title: ConcatTemplate

DialogResponse.description:
How a step answers the JavaScript dialog its action raises.

A browser ``alert``/``confirm``/``prompt``/``beforeunload`` dialog is not a
surface: it is a screen state of the page that raised it, and it blocks
that page until it is answered. On the browser backend the step's action
arms a one-shot answer before delivering input; its recorded kind and
message identify the dialog. Legacy contracts without a kind retain their
message-only behavior. A dialog that does not show exactly ``message`` is
dismissed, never accepted, and the step halts. On a screen-driven backend
(desktop, RDP, Citrix) a dialog is just pixels and is recorded as the
clicks that answer it, so this field is browser-only
(docs/MULTI_SURFACE.md, "Dialogs").

The identity is either the exact ``message`` or ``message_pattern``, a
full-match regex. The compiler writes the pattern whenever the recorded
message carried a demonstrated parameter value or digits (a record
number, a date), so the bundle never seals that value.
DialogResponse.title: DialogResponse

Effect.description:
A typed system-of-record effect (RFC ``Effect``, concrete runtime form).

An ``Effect`` is a *contract*: what must be true of the system of record
for a step to have actually succeeded. It is deliberately substrate-neutral
-- the SAME ``Effect`` is checked by the REST verifier, the FHIR verifier,
or the filesystem verifier (see :class:`EffectVerifier`). The verifier maps
:attr:`match` / :attr:`field` onto its substrate's query language.

Binds to the RFC (``docs/design/WORKFLOW_PROGRAM_IR.md`` section 2.2): the
RFC's ``Effect(kind="record_written", probe="encounter exists for
patient")`` is realized here with a machine-checkable :attr:`match`
selector and an :attr:`expected_count`; the RFC's
``Effect(kind="field_equals", field="note", value=params.note)`` maps to
:attr:`field` / :attr:`value`.
Effect.title: Effect

EffectKind.description:
System-of-record effect kinds (RFC section 2.2).

These are the NEW kinds the RFC adds beyond the vision-checkable
postcondition kinds (``text_present`` / ``region_stable`` / ...): their
probe is a read against the system of record, not the frame.
EffectKind.title: EffectKind

EffectVerificationPolicy.description: Evidence strength assigned to one exact actuation-path effect.
EffectVerificationPolicy.title: EffectVerificationPolicy

EnvironmentBoundary.description: Application/environment scope in which the qualification is valid.
EnvironmentBoundary.title: EnvironmentBoundary

EvidenceRef.description: Local or customer-controlled evidence reference; never evidence content.
EvidenceRef.title: EvidenceRef

FieldSpec.description: One field of a record: its name, kind and how strictly it is read.

name.description: Lower snake case, unique in the schema.
name.title: Name

choices.description: Allowed values; required when kind is enum.
choices.title: Choices

date_order.description: How to read 03/04/2026; unset means ambiguous.
date_order.title: Date Order

pattern.description: Regular expression the normalized value matches.
pattern.title: Pattern

min_confidence.description: Below this the value goes to the review queue; unset means no confidence gate.
min_confidence.title: Min Confidence

proof.description: Overrides the schema's proof for this field.

FieldSpec.title: FieldSpec

FormIdentity.description:
Record identity of a save on a create-new form: the form it submits is
the demonstrated form, holding exactly what this run typed.

A form that creates a record shows no existing record next to its save
button: the record is the one the run is entering. So the save's identity
is the form itself, all of it. The recorder observes, right before the
demonstrated click on a labelled submit button, that the button submits
the one HTML form owning every field typed into since the last save (not
in a table row or a single field's own widget), and fingerprints that
form. Before the click at run time, the replayer requires:

- the button is still that form's submit button, and the form owns
  exactly ``filled_fields`` fields this run typed into, each holding
  exactly what the run typed;
- the form submits to the same origin and path (``action_sha256``) with
  the same ``method``, and would send the same set of control names and
  types (``controls_sha256``), hidden ones included;
- every control the run did not type into (a hidden record or parent id,
  a select left on its default, a checked box) holds the demonstrated
  value: salted digests in ``value_digests``, under ``value_salt`` (the
  identity-template scheme). Hidden tokens are not compared (``exempt``):
  ones named like a token, and ones that changed while the demonstration
  was typed.

Anything else halts before the click. A submit event from any other form
or control during the click is cancelled and halts the run.

Counts, tokens, names and digests only; no field text or value.
FormIdentity.title: FormIdentity

GovernedAuthorizationParameter.description: One value-free parameter declaration in a governed template.
GovernedAuthorizationParameter.title: GovernedAuthorizationParameter

GovernedAuthorizationTemplate.description:
Immutable production authorization shape for one certified bundle.

This is not a bearer capability.  It deliberately excludes runtime input
values, approval identity, credentials, and effect or identity recipes.
The template lives in manifest provenance so it can commit to the final
content digest without creating a content-digest cycle.
GovernedAuthorizationTemplate.title: GovernedAuthorizationTemplate

GradeGate.description: The minimum read grade a write step accepts for the values it writes.

fields.description: Fields the step writes; empty means every field.
fields.title: Fields

GradeGate.title: GradeGate

Guard.description:
A deterministic precondition on a step (RFC §2.2, Phase 1 scope).

``predicate`` is evaluated over the step's entry frame. When it does NOT
hold, ``on_unmet`` decides: ``"halt"`` (the DEFAULT -- the safe direction
for an unmet precondition, per the RFC's refuse-rather-than-guess posture)
stops the run naming the step; ``"skip"`` makes the step a no-op success
(the expected-but-optional case, e.g. dismissing a survey modal only when it
appeared -- a guarded branch WITHOUT the Phase-2 state machine). Full
multi-way branching is Phase 2.
Guard.title: Guard

GuardSource.description:
Why a guard is in the program, when spoken narration suggested it.

Written by induction (``compiler.narration_rules``) for a guard that
started as a narrated proposal and was then certified. The sentence is
scrubbed narration. It explains the guard to a reviewer; the runtime never
reads it.

sentence.description: The scrubbed sentence that suggested it
sentence.title: Sentence

accepted_by.description: Who accepted it, when a person certified it
accepted_by.title: Accepted By

recording.description: Index of the recording the sentence came from
recording.title: Recording

GuardSource.title: GuardSource

HaltCleanup.description:
What a stopped item does to the app's screen before the next item.

A halted item can leave a dialog open, a form half filled or another page
in front. Before the next item runs on the same session, the cleanup's
``steps`` run (each one only when its control is on screen), and then the
``start_state`` must hold. If it doesn't, the session is dirty and takes
no more items (docs/HALT_CLEANUP.md).

Navigation only: no step may save, declare an effect, call an API or type
text. A record the item saved is rollback's job, not this one's.
HaltCleanup.title: HaltCleanup

HaltCleanupQualification.description: The test-copy evidence that a halt cleanup reaches the start screen.
HaltCleanupQualification.title: HaltCleanupQualification

HoverEvidence.description:
What the recording saw when the pointer rested on a click target.

See :mod:`openadapt_flow.runtime.hover_evidence`. Captured for click steps
whose target carries no record identity (an icon-only control) on a
pixel surface. Replay moves the pointer onto the resolved target, waits
``dwell_ms`` and compares its response with this one before clicking.

response.description: Whether anything near the target changed under the pointer
response.title: Response

region.description: The changed box, as an offset from the recorded click point (dx, dy, w, h). Set iff ``response``.
region.title: Region

crop.description: Bundle-relative PNG of the response pixels (templates/hover/), sealed with the other image crops. Set iff ``response``.
crop.title: Crop

HoverEvidence.title: HoverEvidence

IdentityEnforcement.description: Whether the policy names shipped runtime behavior or future intent.
IdentityEnforcement.title: IdentityEnforcement

IdentityNormalizer.description: Explicit, bounded transforms permitted for a normalized comparison.
IdentityNormalizer.title: IdentityNormalizer

IdentityPolicy.description: Quorum policy for one canonical Flow action.
IdentityPolicy.title: IdentityPolicy

IdentitySignalKey.description: Closed, PHI-free semantic keys for qualified identity evidence.
IdentitySignalKey.title: IdentitySignalKey

IdentitySignalPolicy.description: How one semantic identity signal is compared using retained evidence.

extract_pattern.description: Optional explicit regular expression with one named 'value' group. For structured/context text, only that field participates in the identity vote; the semantic key alone never extracts a value.
extract_pattern.title: Extract Pattern

expected_value.description: Qualified PHI-free identifier expected from a dedicated application/session/workflow-state runtime observer.
expected_value.title: Expected Value

params.description: Explicit workflow parameters whose whole demonstrated values are replaced before comparison. No implicit substring inference occurs.
params.title: Params

IdentitySignalPolicy.title: IdentitySignalPolicy

IdentityTemplate.description:
PHI-free stand-in for ``Anchor.context_text`` / ``structured_identity``.

A salted-hash, shape-preserving template of the recorded identity band. It
lets the runtime re-run the SAME wrong-patient identity check
(:mod:`openadapt_flow.runtime.identity_template`) with no readable name /
DOB / MRN in the artifact. NOT a cryptographic control (a salted hash of a
low-entropy identifier is brute-forceable by a holder of the bundle + salt);
it removes *plaintext* PHI. The at-rest control is bundle encryption
(docs/phi_at_rest.md, deferred). Set ``OPENADAPT_FLOW_IDENTITY_SALT`` at
compile+replay to keep the salt out of the bundle and make the hashes
one-way to anyone without the external secret.

ocr_noise.description: Writer-owned salted noise hashes, schema0. Classification-only: can supply glyph uncertainty but never identity authority. Unavailable on parameterized calls.

structured.description: salted hash of the structured identity string
structured.title: Structured

structured_params.description: Workflow parameters embedded in the structured identity. Their demonstrated values are replaced by fixed sentinels before hashing; replay substitutes the run's value before exact compare.
structured_params.title: Structured Params

signal_hashes.description: Salted hashes of strict exact/explicitly-normalized identity evidence, including operator-selected extracted fields. Keys are produced by identity_signals.
signal_hashes.title: Signal Hashes

context_params.description: Workflow parameters replaced by fixed sentinels before the captured-context signal hashes were computed.
context_params.title: Context Params

record_key.description: Salted hash of the stable record id the target's row carried at teach time (app-owned DOM data-* ids, the row link's path). When set, replay acts only on the shown row with the same id.
record_key.title: Record Key

structured_row.description: Whether the structured identity came from a record row at teach time. False lets a replay surface that cannot count look-alike rows still act on the target (a form field, a button); None (unknown) is treated as a row.
structured_row.title: Structured Row

teach_ambiguous.description: Teach time saw another shown row with the same identity and no record id between them. Replay halts before a consequential write: a twin that later scrolls out of view would otherwise pass the text check.
teach_ambiguous.title: Teach Ambiguous

IdentityTemplate.title: IdentityTemplate

Interstitial.description:
A KNOWN recurring interstitial that can appear at a step's entry frame
and would otherwise block the run (docs/LIMITS.md "state dependency").

Examples are a reversible "rate this" modal or a "What's New" release
notice -- overlays that are NOT part of the recorded task but appear
intermittently and, left unhandled, either steal the click (a silent wrong
action) or make the target unresolvable (a babysit-the-queue halt every time
they show). Consent, authentication, submission, and other consequential
prompts are deliberately outside this automatic path.

Detection is model-free: ``detect`` is a Phase-1 :class:`Predicate` (a
``TEXT_PRESENT`` on the overlay's signature text is typical), evaluated over
the settled entry frame with ZERO model calls. Handling is declarative:

- ``dismiss_key`` set -> press Escape to dismiss it, then re-settle and
  verify the declared ``clearance`` predicate.
- ``dismiss_anchor`` set -> resolve+click a non-consequential close control
  via the SAME model-free resolution ladder, then re-settle and verify the
  declared ``clearance`` predicate.
- NEITHER set -> a known BLOCKING interstitial with no safe automatic
  dismissal: the run HALTS gracefully NAMING it (a clear report, not a blind
  "target not found"), so an operator handles it deliberately.

Automatic dismissal is admitted only when ``risk`` is explicitly
``"reversible"``, ``consequential`` is explicitly ``False``, and an
expected visual ``clearance`` predicate is declared. Every attempted
dismissal is recorded in the enclosing :class:`StepResult` before delivery;
a delivery error, failed clearance, or persistent detection HALTs after one
action (no blind retries). Interstitials are
checked at EVERY step's entry, before the guard / wait_until gates, since an
overlay can appear at any point in a workflow, not only at its start.

name.description: Human-readable label for reports/HALT text.
name.title: Name

detect.description: Model-free condition that is TRUE when this interstitial is on the current frame (typically TEXT_PRESENT on its signature text).

dismiss_key.description: Key to press to dismiss it. Only 'Escape' is admitted on the automatic non-consequential path. Mutually exclusive with dismiss_anchor.
dismiss_key.title: Dismiss Key

dismiss_anchor.description: Non-consequential close control to resolve+click. Used when Escape does not dismiss the overlay.

risk.description: Declared dismissal risk. Automatic dismissal requires an explicit 'reversible' declaration.
risk.title: Risk

consequential.description: Whether dismissal can create a consequential state change. Automatic dismissal requires an explicit false declaration.
consequential.title: Consequential

clearance.description: Expected visual postcondition after dismissal. It must hold and the detection predicate must no longer hold before replay continues.

effect_watch.description: Dismiss only under the run's write watchers (openadapt_flow.runtime.effect_watch): the browser's write fence and the system-of-record read-back. A run that can't watch, or any write a watcher sees, halts the run. Set on every interruption class (openadapt_flow.interruptions), declared or learned; it also limits the dismissal to Escape or a control whose label is a closed non-committing one (close, dismiss, not now, continue session).
effect_watch.title: Effect Watch

dialog_title.description: The interruption's accessible title, when an interruption class declares it; the whole dialog must carry it.
dialog_title.title: Dialog Title

Interstitial.title: Interstitial

JobAuthoringBinding.description: Immutable identity/intent only; all five wire fields are required.
JobAuthoringBinding.title: JobAuthoringBinding

JudgmentCaseProvenanceV1.description: The bounded origin of a local case, without an unbounded rationale.
JudgmentCaseProvenanceV1.title: JudgmentCaseProvenanceV1

JudgmentCaseV1.description:
One reviewed example or counterfactual for a typed decision state.

``automatic_rule`` names a reviewed rule and a finite compiled option. It
never embeds an expression, prompt, natural-language reason, or generated
executable program. The runtime continues to use ``BusinessDecisionSpec``.
JudgmentCaseV1.title: JudgmentCaseV1

JudgmentDecisionBindingV1.description: Exact executable decision revision that a local case describes.
JudgmentDecisionBindingV1.title: JudgmentDecisionBindingV1

JudgmentFactFieldV1.description: One typed local fact. Values have no implied policy meaning.
JudgmentFactFieldV1.title: JudgmentFactFieldV1

JudgmentFactSchemaBindingV1.description: One fact schema bound to one exact graph decision node.
JudgmentFactSchemaBindingV1.title: JudgmentFactSchemaBindingV1

JudgmentFactSchemaV1.description: The closed fact vocabulary for one decision state.
JudgmentFactSchemaV1.title: JudgmentFactSchemaV1

Landmark.description:
A stable nearby text element, used by the geometry resolution rung.

``relation`` describes where the LANDMARK sits relative to the target:
a landmark that is ``left_of`` the target implies the target is
``distance_px`` to the landmark's right. ``dx_px``/``dy_px``, when set,
are the exact pixel offsets from the landmark's center to the target
click point (target = landmark_center + (dx_px, dy_px)); the geometry
rung prefers them over the coarser relation/distance estimate.

match_mode.description: OCR comparison mode for this retained relation. Compiler-mined generic context remains fuzzy; a qualified opaque-field label uses exact normalized text so a near label cannot authorize input.
match_mode.title: Match Mode

dx_px.description: Exact x offset landmark center -> target click point
dx_px.title: Dx Px

dy_px.description: Exact y offset landmark center -> target click point
dy_px.title: Dy Px

Landmark.title: Landmark

LocalEvidenceRefV1.description: A local artifact reference. No remote URL or artifact body is allowed.
LocalEvidenceRefV1.title: LocalEvidenceRefV1

LocaleInvariants.description:
Environment facts recorded with a demonstration and checked at replay.

``None`` means the fact could not be read on that computer.

locale.description: BCP-47 / POSIX locale id, e.g. en_US, fr_CA, de_DE.
locale.title: Locale

date_order.description: How the OS orders numeric dates: mdy, dmy, or ymd.
date_order.title: Date Order

keyboard_layout.description: Keyboard layout id as the OS reports it (macOS input source, Windows KLID, or XKB layout[+variant]).
keyboard_layout.title: Keyboard Layout

LocaleInvariants.title: LocaleInvariants

LoopSpec.description:
The body of a ``loop`` state (RFC §2.3; Rousillon / Helena / WebRobot).

Binds a ``relation`` (worklist) and a ``body`` subflow that runs ONCE PER
ROW, the row's fields merged into the run params for that iteration (so an
``entity_ref`` param re-resolves by the identity ladder each pass --
iteration N acts on the RIGHT row, not a recorded pixel position). A
zero-row worklist runs the body ZERO times. Iteration is BOUNDED by
``max_iterations`` -- a worklist longer than the bound HALTs (fail-safe),
never runs unbounded.

relation.description: Name of the Relation / worklist to loop
relation.title: Relation

var.description: Optional human label for the loop variable (for reports)
var.title: Var

LoopSpec.title: LoopSpec

NativeSelectContract.description: Exact semantic selection, distinct from remote text-and-key input.
NativeSelectContract.title: NativeSelectContract

NativeSelectOption.description: One option in a bounded, observed native HTML select census.
NativeSelectOption.title: NativeSelectOption

OptionChoice.description:
Choose one option of a dropdown by what it says, then read it back.

One model for every dropdown family (docs/CHOICES.md):

- ``native_select``: an HTML ``<select>``. The option is set through the
  DOM and the control's selected option is read back.
- ``listed_option``: anything that opens a list of options when the
  control is clicked (ARIA listboxes, ``<div>`` lists, searchable selects,
  type-aheads whose options load from the server). Replay clicks the
  control, types the wanted label when the demonstration typed a search
  (``query="label"``), waits until the option list stops changing, and
  clicks the one option whose label (or ``value`` attribute) equals the
  wanted value. The control must then show that label (``readback``).

The wanted value is the step's parameter when it has one, else ``label``.
No option, more than one, or a disabled one halts the step before the
option is clicked; a control that does not show the choice afterwards
halts it too. Position never decides which option is chosen.
OptionChoice.title: OptionChoice

ParamKind.description:
Typed-parameter kinds (RFC §2.2 ``ParamSpec.type``).

``entity_ref`` names an ENTITY to be re-resolved by the identity ladder at
run time (the "which patient" fix, docs/LIMITS.md), not a literal to blindly
substitute; the other kinds are literal values. Phase 1 stores the type for
typing/validation/emit -- kind-specific run-time resolution (entity_ref
re-resolution) is Phase 2+.
ParamKind.title: ParamKind

ParamSpec.description:
A TYPED workflow parameter (RFC §2.2). Supersedes a bare
``params: dict[str, str]`` entry by carrying a type, the recorded demo
value (``example``, which doubles as the replay default), whether it is
required, and enum choices. Additive: ``Workflow.param_specs`` lives
ALONGSIDE the frozen ``Workflow.params`` dict; a bundle with an empty
``param_specs`` behaves exactly as before.

``intake_field`` (optional) names the intake document field this tool
parameter may come from. When set, the MCP/runtime gate refuses a call
whose value does not match the trusted intake provenance for that field
(#1890). Unset means the parameter is not intake-bound.

example.description: Recorded demo value; also the replay default when the caller supplies no value for this parameter.
example.title: Example

choices.description: Allowed values for an enum param.
choices.title: Choices

intake_field.description: Intake field name this parameter may be filled from. When set, a taught-tool call must match the registered intake provenance for that field, or it is refused.
intake_field.title: Intake Field

ParamSpec.title: ParamSpec

PixelsOnlyPass.description: The qualification pass run with structure lookups disabled.
PixelsOnlyPass.title: PixelsOnlyPass

template.description: Bundle-relative PNG crop of the expected REGION_STABLE content; lets the check tolerate small layout shifts (content found near, not exactly at, the recorded region)
template.title: Template

Predicate.description:
A deterministic condition over observed state (RFC §2.2 ``Predicate``).

Used two ways in Phase 1: as a ``Step.wait_until`` readiness predicate (the
replayer polls it, BOUNDED by ``timeout_s``, and HALTS on timeout -- never
proceeds-anyway) and as the condition inside a ``Guard``. Model-free by
construction (see ``runtime.replayer._predicate_holds``); an unknown kind
fails safe (does not hold).

intent.description: Human-readable label (also the resolution-ladder intent for an ANCHOR_RESOLVES predicate).
intent.title: Intent

timeout_s.description: wait_until bound: how long the replayer polls this predicate before HALTing (fail-safe; never proceed-anyway).
timeout_s.title: Timeout S

Predicate.title: Predicate

PredicateKind.description:
Deterministic, model-free predicate kinds (RFC §2.2 ``Predicate``).

A predicate is evaluated over the CURRENT observed frame / run parameters
with ZERO model calls -- it is the thing a linear IR cannot express. Phase 1
ships the concrete kinds needed to (a) subsume today's SCROLL closed loop
(``anchor_resolves``), (b) turn the optional-modal case into a guarded
branch (``text_present``), and (c) branch on a parameter (``param_equals``),
plus boolean composition. ``worklist_nonempty`` (loops) is Phase 2.
PredicateKind.title: PredicateKind

ProgramGraph.description:
A directed graph of :class:`State`s with a single ``entry`` (RFC §2.2).

Used both as the top-level program (``Workflow.program``) and as a reusable
subflow (``Workflow.subflows[name]``, or a ``loop`` body). Walked state by
state from ``entry`` until a terminal (or, for a subflow, until it falls off
/ reaches a ``success`` terminal, which RETURNS to the caller).
ProgramGraph.title: ProgramGraph

QualificationActionTarget.description: One exact workflow action and actuation path exercised by a case.
QualificationActionTarget.title: QualificationActionTarget

QualificationCase.description:
A representative or deterministic fault case.

``input_ref`` names a customer-controlled parameter fixture.  Parameter
values and secrets do not enter the qualification project.
QualificationCase.title: QualificationCase

QualificationCaseResult.description: One runner-produced result for a qualification case.
QualificationCaseResult.title: QualificationCaseResult

QualificationProject.description: Versioned qualification configuration sealed inside a Flow bundle.
QualificationProject.title: QualificationProject

QualifiedBusinessDecisionContextCard.description: One reviewed static context item for a mobile decision.
QualifiedBusinessDecisionContextCard.title: QualifiedBusinessDecisionContextCard

QualifiedBusinessDecisionDelivery.description: Reviewed mobile-delivery contract for one exact graph decision.
QualifiedBusinessDecisionDelivery.title: QualifiedBusinessDecisionDelivery

QualifiedBusinessDecisionOptionCopy.description: Optional reviewed detail for one already-declared finite option.
QualifiedBusinessDecisionOptionCopy.title: QualifiedBusinessDecisionOptionCopy

QualifiedEffectRequirement.description: One exact qualified effect-strength requirement admitted for a run.
QualifiedEffectRequirement.title: QualifiedEffectRequirement

QualifiedEntityLabel.description:
An optional local presentation label for one qualified step.

Qualification and execution do not require this label. Reviewed labels can
cross a remote boundary. A custom label remains local and remote consumers
receive its signed neutral ``record`` or ``item`` fallback.
QualifiedEntityLabel.title: QualifiedEntityLabel

QualifiedLookup.description:
What a qualification's lookups ran on, kept in the qualification project.

``capabilities_used`` is read from the run reports of the signed cases.
``surface`` is the deployment surface the qualification was for.
QualifiedLookup.title: QualifiedLookup

ReadProof.description: Which proof to collect for a read. Everything is off by default.

double_read.description: Read through two channels and compare.
double_read.title: Double Read

committed_readback.description: Close, reopen by identity fields and read again.
committed_readback.title: Committed Readback

seal.description: Cover the value with a signed Seal.
seal.title: Seal

ReadProof.title: ReadProof

ReadStepSpec.description:
What a READ step reads and how much proof it collects.

``region`` is the field's value box on the recorded frame. When the step
has an ``anchor`` (usually the field's label), the runtime re-resolves it
on the live frame and moves ``region`` by the same offset, so the read
follows the field when the layout shifts. Without an anchor, ``region`` is
used as recorded.

Proof is opt-in (:class:`~openadapt_flow.records.schema.ReadProof`): by
default one channel is read (the clipboard when the runtime has one,
otherwise OCR), the value is ``unchecked`` and carries no Seal. OCR and
the clipboard are deterministic channels; a READ step makes no model
calls.

schema_name.description: The RecordSchema this field belongs to.
schema_name.title: Schema Name

copy_keys.description: Keys pressed to copy the focused field for a clipboard read.
copy_keys.title: Copy Keys

on_review.description: What to do when the read needs review (channels disagree, an invalid value, a missing second channel). ``halt`` stops the run and asks a person; ``continue`` records the field for the review queue and goes on.
on_review.title: On Review

ReadStepSpec.title: ReadStepSpec

ReadbackAdmission.description:
A person's acceptance of a read-back taught by demonstration.

The demonstration that taught the check cannot approve it. Until a person
admits it, the check can't confirm a save (the verifier rules
``INDETERMINATE``). The admission is bound to the exact check by
:attr:`spec_digest`; a changed check needs a new admission.
ReadbackAdmission.title: ReadbackAdmission

ReadbackField.description:
One field a person marked on the saved record's screen.

The verifier reads :attr:`region` and requires :attr:`value` there.
ReadbackField.title: ReadbackField

ReadbackGuard.description:
What a read-back's replayed navigation must never do.

The navigation runs in the acting session, on any surface (a browser, a
desktop app, an RDP or Citrix window), where no network guard can stop a
stray write. Before each click the verifier reads the text under the
pointer and refuses a control whose label is a commit word or one of the
save's own control labels; it refuses save and delete key chords. A
refusal makes the check INDETERMINATE (HALT), never a guessed CONFIRM.
ReadbackGuard.title: ReadbackGuard

ReadbackNav.description:
One deterministic navigation action to RE-OPEN the written record by a
path DIFFERENT from the write flow, before an on-screen read-back.

Auto-derived from the demonstration (the steps the person took to view the
saved record again — e.g. clear the form, search the patient, open the
encounter). Deliberately tiny and model-free: a re-navigation is replayed
by coordinate/keyboard exactly as recorded; anything a backend cannot
perform makes the read-back INDETERMINATE (HALT), never a guessed CONFIRM.
ReadbackNav.title: ReadbackNav

ReadbackReference.description:
A reference number the application shows right after the save.

Learned from the demonstration: text that appeared on the screen the save
left, was not typed, and looks like an identifier (a claim, order or
encounter number). Read at run time from :attr:`region` with
:attr:`pattern` (one capture group), it is evidence that the application
issued a record (check level ``same_screen``) and, when a navigation
step types it (:attr:`ReadbackNav.reference`), the way to find the record
again. The captured value itself is never stored in a report.
ReadbackReference.title: ReadbackReference

ReadbackReset.description:
The step of a demonstrated check that throws away client-side state.

Without one, the check could read a form buffer or a client-side page the
save left behind, and a save that never reached the record would pass.
ReadbackReset.title: ReadbackReset

ReadbackSpec.description:
The on-screen read-back oracle mined from the demonstration.

Carries WHERE to re-read the saved value (:attr:`region`) and, for the
stronger DIFFERENT-PATH variant, the re-navigation that re-opens the record
(:attr:`renavigation`) so the read is forced through a real fetch rather
than the form the write left on screen. Consumed by
:class:`~openadapt_flow.runtime.effects.onscreen.OnScreenReadbackVerifier`;
every non-onscreen substrate ignores it.

SAFETY — the ``different_path`` flag is the gate. A ``different_path=True``
read-back re-opens the record by an independent path (defeating the
"the form still shows what I typed but nothing persisted" phantom-save
class) and is safe enough to be the DEFAULT out-of-the-box oracle. A
``different_path=False`` (SAME-SURFACE) read-back re-reads the very region
the write drove; it CANNOT see a phantom/optimistic save (the measured
false-CONFIRM rate is > 0), so it is wired but NON-default — a
halt-inducing consistency signal an operator opts into with eyes open, not
a pass. See ``docs/LIMITS.md`` and ``benchmark/effect_readback/``.
ReadbackSpec.title: ReadbackSpec

RegistryOrigin.description:
Where a bundle pulled from the skills registry came from.

Part of the workflow content, so the content digest covers it: a bundle
that says it came from the registry runs only with a certification bound
to its own digest and environment (``openadapt_flow.skills``). Removing
it makes a different, unverified local bundle.
RegistryOrigin.title: RegistryOrigin

Relation.description:
A worklist a ``loop`` state iterates over (RFC §2.3).

Variable-length ``rows``; each row is a mapping of param name -> value that
is bound into the run params in scope for that loop iteration. Rows may be
INLINED here (deterministic, $0 -- the authored/compiled case) or supplied
at run time (``Replayer.run(worklists=...)``) for a genuinely data-dependent
queue whose length is unknown until run time. Either way iteration stays
BOUNDED (see :class:`LoopSpec.max_iterations`).

rows.description: Inline worklist rows; each binds params for one iteration
rows.title: Rows

Relation.title: Relation

RequalificationCondition.description: A bounded condition that invalidates this qualification.
RequalificationCondition.title: RequalificationCondition

State.description:
A node in the workflow-program graph (RFC §2.2).

Its ``kind`` selects the payload: ``action`` carries a hardened Phase-1
:class:`Step`; ``branch`` picks an edge purely by guard;
``business_decision`` binds one authorized finite human choice; ``loop``
iterates a worklist; ``subflow_call`` invokes a reusable subgraph;
``terminal`` ends the (sub)graph. ``transitions`` are the outgoing edges
(empty on a terminal, a single unconditional edge on a degenerate linear
node). ``on_exception`` routes a FAILED action to a local handler instead
of aborting the whole run.
State.title: State

StateKind.description: The kinds of node in a workflow-program graph (RFC §2.2).
StateKind.title: StateKind

intent.description: Human-readable purpose of the step
intent.title: Intent

secret.description: TYPE steps only: the parameter is a SECRET (e.g. a password). Its literal value is NEVER stored in the recording, the events log, or this bundle; at replay it is injected from the environment variable OPENADAPT_FLOW_SECRET_<PARAM> (the param name upper-cased). ``text`` is always None for a secret step, and ``param`` names the required secret. A missing secret at replay is a clear, fail-fast error (see runtime.Replayer).
secret.title: Secret

field_label.description: TYPE/SELECT_OPTION steps only: the receiving field's best available label, captured PASSIVELY at record time (DOM <label>/aria-label/placeholder/name for web; accessibility label for native where the seam exists; nearby-OCR text as a compile-time fallback). Pure evidence for the compile-time parameter-proposal pass and the operator confirm review -- NEVER read at replay, and never a source of silent parameterization: a label-derived parameter proposal is always gated behind operator confirmation (see compiler.annotate.FieldLabelAnnotator).
field_label.title: Field Label

choice.description: SELECT_OPTION only: choose the option by its label or value and read the control back (OptionChoice). The wanted value is params[param] when param is set, else text.

selection_commit_key.description: SELECT_OPTION only: the Enter/Tab commit key compiled from a demonstrated provisional type-ahead followed immediately by that key. Runtime delivers text+commit as one backend operation and verifies the selected value in selection_region.
selection_commit_key.title: Selection Commit Key

selection_region.description: Exact demonstrated readback band where the complete option value was readable after commit. Runtime maps this band relative to the freshly re-resolved anchor; its recorded absolute coordinates are never replayed directly.
selection_region.title: Selection Region

target_param.description: CLICK/DOUBLE_CLICK only: the run parameter whose value names the record this click selects (a search result, a worklist row). When the run's value differs from the demonstrated one, the runtime looks for the run's value instead of the demonstrated label and skips the demonstrated crop; the identity check then verifies the row in parameter mode. A step without identity evidence, or with an empty value, halts before acting. None (the default) clicks the demonstrated target, as before.
target_param.title: Target Param

modifiers.description: HOTKEY modifiers in deterministic press order
modifiers.title: Modifiers

drag_end_anchor.description: DRAG destination evidence, resolved independently on the same fresh pre-actuation frame as the source anchor

risk_explanation.description: Why the compiler or qualifying operator assigned this risk. This is provenance, not runtime evidence.
risk_explanation.title: Risk Explanation

risk_review_required.description: True when risk is ambiguous and certification must refuse until an operator supplies an explicit reviewed override
risk_review_required.title: Risk Review Required

surface.description: Id of the declared surface (Workflow.surfaces) this step runs on; for SWITCH_SURFACE, the surface it switches TO. None means the primary surface.
surface.title: Surface

opens.description: Ids of the page surfaces this step's action opens (new tabs, popups), in the order the browser created them. At replay the step must open exactly these pages; any other new page halts.
opens.title: Opens

surface_origin.description: SWITCH_SURFACE to a browser surface: the exact scheme://host[:port] the target page showed when the demonstration switched to it.
surface_origin.title: Surface Origin

closes_surface.description: A click on a page surface (a popup or tab a step opened) that closed that page in the demonstration, such as an approval window's final button. At replay, the browser backend may then count the click as delivered when the browser reports the page closed during the click and the page is confirmed closed. Without it, that error leaves delivery uncertain.
closes_surface.title: Closes Surface

dialog.description: Browser backend: the JavaScript dialog this step's action raises, answered by the backend when its message matches exactly.

identity_armed.description: Clicks/anchored TYPE/SELECT_OPTION only: True when the pre-click identity check is armed (context band recorded); False when the step will click WITHOUT identity verification; None for steps the check does not apply to (or pre-metric bundles).
identity_armed.title: Identity Armed

identity_unarmed_reason.description: Why an applicable step compiled unarmed (no readable band text, band too generic, ...); None when armed or not applicable.
identity_unarmed_reason.title: Identity Unarmed Reason

identifier_crop_missing_reason.description: Why this identity-applicable step compiled WITHOUT a pixel identifier crop (anchor.identifier_crop) — the explicit degrade record for the pixel identity tier, mirroring identity_unarmed_reason: e.g. structured identity owns the step, no readable identity band, a marked --identifier region was invalid. None when a crop WAS emitted, on non-applicable steps, and on bundles compiled before this field existed. Without a crop the pixel-compare tier abstains on remote-display/pixel replays and identity falls to the OCR band tier (docs/LIMITS.md).
identifier_crop_missing_reason.title: Identifier Crop Missing Reason

hover.description: Pointer-hover response captured at record time for a click whose target carries no record identity (runtime.hover_evidence). None when the recorder could not hover or the step has other identity evidence, and on bundles compiled before this field.

submit_binding.description: Consequential CLICK/DOUBLE_CLICK on an unlabeled control only: the recorded structural binding of that control to the form whose fields the demonstration filled (see SubmitBinding). The replayer verifies the same binding on the live page before it clicks and refuses when it differs or is ambiguous. None on other steps and on bundles compiled before this field existed.

submit_binding_unbound_reason.description: Why a consequential click on an unlabeled control could not be bound to the form it submits (for example, two unlabeled controls follow the filled fields). The replayer refuses that click. None when bound, not applicable, or the recording carried no DOM evidence for the control.
submit_binding_unbound_reason.title: Submit Binding Unbound Reason

StructuralLocator.description:
A stable structural (DOM / accessibility) locator for a step's target.

Captured at record time from the recording backend's structured layer
(:meth:`openadapt_flow.backend.StructuralActionBackend.structural_locator_at`)
and consumed at replay by the structural ACTION rung -- the TOP of the
resolution ladder (:mod:`openadapt_flow.runtime.resolver`). The runtime
re-finds the SAME element by its stable identity -- a DOM id / CSS selector
/ ARIA role+name, or a Windows UIA ``AutomationId`` / ``ControlType``+
``Name`` -- and acts on the element's center DETERMINISTICALLY, with no
pixel matching. This is the thesis shift from "vision-only" to
"deterministic compiled automation with visual FALLBACK": the desktop
benchmark measured UIA execution 21/21 vs compiled visual replay 6/21 under
render drift.

The visual anchor (template / ocr_text / landmarks) is ALWAYS kept too: the
ladder falls through to it UNCHANGED when this locator is absent (pixel-only
substrate -- RDP/Citrix/canvas) or when the element cannot be located at
replay (see docs/LIMITS.md). Structural resolution is ADDITIVE -- it never
removes the visual floor.

Fields are backend-neutral; a browser backend fills ``selector`` / ``role``
/ ``name`` from the DOM, a native backend fills ``automation_id`` / ``role``
/ ``name`` from its accessibility tree (Windows UIA AutomationId or the
Linux AT-SPI accessible ID). Each backend uses whichever fields it
recorded; unset fields are ignored.

frame_path.description: Outermost-to-innermost CSS selectors for iframe/frame elements containing a browser target. Each selector must resolve uniquely in its parent frame; absent means the top-level document.
frame_path.title: Frame Path

name.description: Accessible name / label / text of the target element
name.title: Name

automation_id.description: Stable native accessibility ID: Windows UIA AutomationId or Linux AT-SPI accessible ID
automation_id.title: Automation Id

window_name.description: Exact top-level accessibility window name captured with the target. Native backends use it to scope candidate enumeration and refuse duplicate controls in a different application window.
window_name.title: Window Name

StructuralLocator.title: StructuralLocator

SubmitBinding.description:
Compile-time binding of an unlabeled submit control to its form.

An icon-only Save (no text, accessible name, or tooltip) that is not in a
table row has no record identity of its own, so a consequential click on
it cannot be tied to a record the usual way (by the row's identity). This
binding ties it to the record the program itself entered instead: the
fields the demonstration typed into before the click.

The recorder observes the DOM immediately before the demonstrated click,
and the compiler keeps the binding only when it is unambiguous:

- **Form ownership.** The control and every filled field share one HTML
  form owner (``shared``); or the fields share a form and the control sits
  outside every form (``fields_only``, a floating Save rendered next to
  the form); or neither the fields nor the control have a form owner
  (``none``). A control owned by another form, or fields spread over more
  than one form, are never bound.
- **Submit role.** ``form_submit`` (a submit button of that form),
  ``form_control`` (another button inside it), or ``detached`` (a button
  outside any form), plus the control's own tag, type, and role, and a
  SHA-256 of its icon geometry (SVG path data, image size, or glyph code
  points; never text or URLs).
- **Position relative to those fields.** The control follows every filled
  field in document order, its centre lies in the same quadrant of the
  fields' bounding box, and the tag path from the binding scope (the
  shared form, or the nearest element that contains the control and the
  fields) down to the control is unchanged.
- **Uniqueness.** Exactly one rendered, unlabeled control follows the
  filled fields inside that scope. Controls in table rows or list items,
  which have row identity, and the adornments inside one field's own
  widget are not counted.

Every field here is a closed-vocabulary token, a count, a boolean, or a
digest, so the binding carries no record content.

At run time the replayer recomputes the same observation for the element
at the freshly resolved point, against the fields that run typed into, and
clicks only when every recorded field matches and the control is still
the only unlabeled control after those fields. The browser re-checks the
same observation at delivery, after the actionability trial, so a change
in between refuses the click.

icon_sha256.description: SHA-256 of the control's icon geometry (SVG path data and shape attributes, image intrinsic size, glyph code points). None when the control draws no vector, image, or glyph content.
icon_sha256.title: Icon Sha256

fixed_position.description: The control or an ancestor is position: fixed or sticky.
fixed_position.title: Fixed Position

filled_fields.description: Distinct fields the demonstration had typed into, still on the page, when it clicked. A run must have typed into the same number of fields, all inside the same scope.
filled_fields.title: Filled Fields

field_step_ids.description: The demonstration's typing steps before this click, for review. Run time verifies the field count and scope, not these ids.
field_step_ids.title: Field Step Ids

SubmitBinding.title: SubmitBinding

SurfaceSpec.description:
One surface a multi-surface workflow runs on.

Three shapes, distinguished by their fields:

- the PRIMARY surface: the first entry, the backend the run is started
  with (``opened_by_step`` is None);
- a PAGE surface: a browser tab or popup that a recorded step opened
  (``opened_by_step`` names that step). At replay it is identified by the
  step that opened it, its position among the pages that step opened, the
  opener relation, its origin, and full-match URL/title patterns;
- a BACKEND surface: another backend the caller supplies by id (a native
  app, an RDP/Citrix window, another browser). ``opened_by_step`` is None
  and the runtime refuses to switch to it unless the supplied backend is of
  the declared ``kind``.

The URL and title patterns can echo application content, so they live only
inside ``workflow.json`` (sealed with it when the bundle is encrypted) and
are never copied into a manifest, run report, or refusal message.

opener_link.description: PAGE surfaces: 'window_opener' when the recorded page's window.opener was the opener surface's page (window.open, or a link without noopener); 'none' when it had no opener (a target=_blank link, which implies noopener). Replay requires the same relation.
opener_link.title: Opener Link

origin.description: PAGE surfaces: exact scheme://host[:port] at open time.
origin.title: Origin

url_pattern.description: PAGE surfaces: regular expression the page URL must FULLY match when it is claimed. Recorded parameter values are generalized.
url_pattern.title: Url Pattern

title_pattern.description: PAGE surfaces: optional full-match regex for the title.
title_pattern.title: Title Pattern

SurfaceSpec.title: SurfaceSpec

TokenTemplate.description:
Salted-hash + shape descriptor for one recorded identity-band token.

Carries NO plaintext (the PHI audit's REM-2): ``c``/``r`` are salted hashes
of the token's OCR-canonical and squashed-raw forms; the rest are
non-identifying shape flags and a length. Enough to reproduce the
wrong-patient guard's per-token budgets at replay
(:mod:`openadapt_flow.runtime.identity_template`) without persisting the
identifier itself.

r.description: salted hash of squashed raw token
r.title: R

bearing.description: identity-bearing (identity.identity_bearing); None in bundles compiled before the flag, which count every token
bearing.title: Bearing

label.description: Writer-owned generic UI-label role from the same raw/comparison token pair as bearing; unknown in older templates
label.title: Label

TokenTemplate.title: TokenTemplate

Transition.description:
A guarded edge to a target state (RFC §2.2) -- the thing a linear IR
cannot express.

``guard`` is a Phase-1 :class:`Predicate` evaluated (model-free) over the
current frame / run params; ``None`` means UNCONDITIONAL (the RFC's ``TRUE``
edge -- the default fall-through, and the only edge kind a degenerate linear
program has). A state's ``transitions`` are evaluated IN ORDER; the first
whose guard holds wins. Multiple non-``TRUE`` transitions make a multi-way
branch.

target.description: Id of the state this edge leads to
target.title: Target

label.description: Human-readable edge label
label.title: Label

Transition.title: Transition

UndoLocate.description:
How an undo finds the record the save created.

Before the save runs, the replayer keeps the ids of the records that
already match :attr:`match` (``<run-dir>/undo/prior/<step>.json``). At undo
time, the one matching record whose id is not in that list is the record
the save created; its id is bound to the run parameter :attr:`param`.
Zero or several such records refuse the undo. See docs/AFTER_A_STOP.md.
UndoLocate.title: UndoLocate

UndoProposal.description:
A compiler-proposed undo that passed verification on a test copy.

Flow offers it after a stop only once a person has approved it
(:attr:`approved_by`), and every run of it still needs that person's
approval at the time it runs. ``evidence_sha256`` binds the verification
record kept in the bundle (``evidence_path``).
UndoProposal.title: UndoProposal

UndoRestore.description:
Which values to keep before a field edit so its undo can restore them.

Before the save runs, the replayer reads the one record matching
:attr:`match` and keeps each named field's value. At undo time each value
is bound to its run parameter, and the undo writes it back.
UndoRestore.title: UndoRestore

UndoStep.description:
A declared compensating action for one step's effect.

For example: "delete the draft row that step ``save_draft`` added". Flow
never runs it on its own. After a stop, the run's change ledger names the
steps that may have changed the app; when one of them has a declared undo,
Flow offers it to a person. It runs only after that person approves it
(``openadapt_flow.after_stop``), and it counts as done only when the
effects declared on its own steps are confirmed in the system of record.

The undo is part of the sealed bundle content: editing it changes the
bundle digest. See ``docs/AFTER_A_STOP.md``.
UndoStep.title: UndoStep

ValueExpr.description:
A single effect-contract value: either a static ``literal`` or a
reference to a run ``param`` (P0-3 fix).

Before this type an :class:`Effect` carried plain static strings, so a
PARAMETERIZED workflow verified its effects against the values baked in at
DEMONSTRATION time (write patient "Susan" via the GUI, then verify the
recorded demo patient "Phil"). ``ValueExpr`` lets a compiled effect declare
``{"param": "patient_id"}`` and have the runtime resolve it against the
RUN's params before verification, so the record actually written is the
record checked.

Exactly one of :attr:`literal` / :attr:`param` is meaningful. Old bundles
(and hand-authored effects) that pass a bare string are coerced to
``ValueExpr(literal=...)`` by :class:`Effect`'s validators, and this type's
``__eq__`` / ``__str__`` compare/render as that bare string so every
existing reader (learning gate signatures, codegen review comments) and the
substrate matchers behave BYTE-FOR-BYTE identically for a literal.
ValueExpr.title: ValueExpr

VerificationTier.description:
Strength of evidence for a declared business effect.

Lower values are stronger. These numbers are a persisted wire value; use
:attr:`check_level` (``openadapt_flow.check_level``, higher is stronger)
to compare with Seal tiers or show the strength to a person. Verifiers
advertise strength explicitly; callers never infer it from class names,
substrate labels, or prose.
VerificationTier.title: VerificationTier

WebFormField.description:
One field of a recorded form save, and where its value comes from.

``param``: a run parameter typed into the form. ``select_label``: a select
whose option is chosen by the label in ``param`` (the value is looked up in
the live form each run). ``session``: a value the server issued to this
session, such as a CSRF token, read from the live form each run.
``form_default``: the form's own default, which must still equal ``value``
in the live form or the API step does not run. ``submitter``: the
``name=value`` the browser adds for the submit button the person clicked;
the live form must still have exactly one enabled submit button that
sends exactly ``value``. ``empty_file``: a file input sent with no file
(a multipart save); the live form must still have that file input, and
the API step never attaches a file.
WebFormField.title: WebFormField

WebFormPrecheck.description:
A read-only request the page made before the save, and its pass rule.

Carries over a check the GUI program made on screen before saving (for
example a duplicate search that must say "No matches were found."). The
response must contain every ``require_text`` or the API step does not
send the save.
WebFormPrecheck.title: WebFormPrecheck

WebFormSpec.description:
How to repeat a recorded browser form save as one HTTP request.

Compiled from the network traffic captured during ``record
--capture-network``. The request goes through the replaying browser's
own session (its cookies), so no credential is stored or needed. Before
sending, the runtime reads ``form_path`` again and refuses (falls back to
the GUI steps) if the form's fields, defaults, options or client-side
rules differ from the recording.
WebFormSpec.title: WebFormSpec

WebFormWrite.description:
A request, other than the save, that wrote while the replaced steps ran.

The API step's span is a declared, ordered sequence: these writes in the
order they were recorded, then the save. Each is one of two roles:

- ``ambient``: the page sent it on its own. It came from a script of
  another document than the form, one that was loaded before the form
  opened (for example an app's tab shell that posts
  ``execute_background_services.php`` on a timer), and the form page's
  source doesn't name it. No replaced step caused it, so the API step
  neither sends nor waits for it; the live page goes on as it does under
  the GUI steps. Listed for the person who admits the step.
- ``step``: a replaced step caused it. The API step sends it, rebuilt
  from ``fields`` the same way as the save, in its recorded place before
  the save. Its read-back is the record check declared on ``from_step``,
  which the binding's record check includes; admission refuses a step
  write whose step has none. A write that fails, or whose response is
  outside ``expected_status``, stops the run with nothing after it sent,
  nothing retried and nothing redone through the GUI, and the run
  reconciles by reading the records back.
WebFormWrite.title: WebFormWrite

validation.description:
Compiled workflow program with linear compatibility and graph execution.

``steps`` preserves the original straight-line bundle format. ``program``,
when present, is the canonical state machine; its action states reuse the
same identity, risk, resolution, postcondition, and effect contracts.

dialogs_recorded.description: The recording captured every browser dialog the demonstration met (docs/CHOICES.md). A run of such a program stops on a dialog no step expects (dialog_unexpected); older programs keep the browser's default dismissal.
dialogs_recorded.title: Dialogs Recorded

secret_params.description: Names of SECRET parameters (e.g. passwords). Their values are NEVER stored here or in ``params``; each is injected at replay from OPENADAPT_FLOW_SECRET_<PARAM> (see Step.secret).
secret_params.title: Secret Params

validation.title: Workflow
